pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:935 Recovery checks heartbeat staleness during selection but omits it from the subsequent update, allowing a refreshed live attempt to be requeued and its target exclusion released.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:570 Queue publication uses SQLite transactions and WAL rather than application-managed replacement of a shared document.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:840 Completion atomically compares the carried attempt against the incumbent running row; fail, heartbeat and checkpoint writes also carry attempt predicates.
crates/core/src/store_instrument.rs:632 The measured operation executes its own future; this queue path does not publish a shared in-flight completion handle.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1553 The reaper selects stale rows separately from their later mutation; intervening awaits allow heartbeat changes that the mutation never revalidates.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:1445 Although claims use shared atomic SQL, boot recovery selects every running job without process ownership or heartbeat freshness, so another process's live job can be reclaimed.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1523 This is an individual job-attempt fence, not a cluster lease controlling the store's general right to write.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:170 The guard uses an app-declared target identity separately from enqueue idempotency and attempt identity; NULL explicitly opts out.

crates/core/migrations/0011_idempotency.sql:5 The unique index atomically deduplicates supplied intent keys; enqueue_dedup returns the existing job with created=false, including after a concurrent insert race.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:567 The queue uses SQLite rather than a replicated log whose leadership admits writes.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:935 reap_stale checks the heartbeat cutoff only in its SELECT; the later fail update can still succeed after a heartbeat refresh because status and attempt remain unchanged.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1520 Renewal belongs to one job attempt; the standard explicitly reserves this technique for the cluster's right-to-write lease.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:805 Claims are exclusive transactional SQL updates, not shared-reader and exclusive-writer announcements over per-key conditional storage.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:717 Target collisions use a centralized queue policy, but enqueue has no queue-depth bound and queued jobs have no maximum wait or expiry.
